_comment: What each rule checks, in plain English, one entry per code in the backend registry. Created and topped up by draft-descriptions.mjs, so this file never needs maintaining by hand: a rule with no entry gets a draft marked "drafted": true, which the skill then has the model rewrite before publishing. Entries without that flag are settled prose and are never regenerated, which is what keeps a no-change run free of model work. Keep "checks" to one or two sentences on the condition; no remedies, no code identifiers, and no numbers. State a threshold by naming its constant in "tolerance" (optionally with wording in "toleranceIs") and the build extracts the value from the code, so a tolerance can never drift and a renamed constant fails the build instead of publishing a stale figure.

GPKG_INVALID_FILE.checks: The upload cannot be opened as a database at all. Usually something that is not a GeoPackage — a shapefile, a zip, a spreadsheet — or a .gpkg truncated by an interrupted copy.

GPKG_NOT_A_GEOPACKAGE.checks: The file opens as a database but is not stamped as a GeoPackage. Typically a SpatiaLite or plain SQLite database given a .gpkg name; the stamp is inside the file, so renaming the extension does not help.

GPKG_MISSING_SYSTEM_TABLE.checks: One of the GeoPackage's own internal housekeeping tables is absent, so the file is broken at the format level rather than merely wrong. Reported once per missing table.

GPKG_MISSING_LAYER.checks: A layer the template requires is absent. Habitats and Red Line Boundary are both required; a layer that exists under a different name counts as missing.

GPKG_UNEXPECTED_FEATURE_LAYER.checks: The file carries a vector mapping layer the template does not list — a constraints layer, a site plan, a working copy. Raster and tile layers are not examined, so an embedded basemap is not caught.

GPKG_BASELINE_SRS_ID.checks: A layer is not in British National Grid (EPSG:27700), or no usable coordinate system number can be read for it. Latitude and longitude and Web Mercator are both rejected. Reported once per layer.

GPKG_BASELINE_GPKG_SRS_INCONSISTENT.checks: The file records one layer's coordinate system in two places and the two disagree. A GIS package will display such a layer without complaint.

GPKG_BASELINE_CONTENTS_DATA_TYPE.checks: A layer is registered as something other than a vector mapping layer. Believed unreachable in practice: only layers already registered as mapping layers are ever examined.

GPKG_BASELINE_INVALID_GEOMETRY_COLUMN_NA.checks: The column holding a layer's shapes has a name containing something other than letters, digits and underscores. The name itself is not compared against the template — only its validity.

GPKG_BASELINE_MULTIPLE_GEOMETRY_COLUMNS.checks: A layer has more than one column holding shapes, either in its registration or in the table itself. Usually the result of a merge or join carrying a second geometry across.

GPKG_BASELINE_GEOMETRY_TYPE_NAME.checks: A layer's declared shape type differs from the template, regardless of what was actually drawn. Habitats must be declared MultiPolygon and Red Line Boundary Polygon — the two required layers want opposite things.

GPKG_BASELINE_GEOMETRY_REGISTRATION_MISS.checks: A layer is listed as a mapping layer but the file never records which of its columns holds the shapes, so no GIS tool can draw it. Applies to the optional layers; the two required layers have their own rules.

GPKG_HABITATS_NO_GEOMETRY_COLUMN.checks: The same missing registration, reported specifically for the Habitats layer.

GPKG_RLB_NO_GEOMETRY_COLUMN.checks: The same missing registration, reported specifically for the Red Line Boundary layer.

GPKG_BASELINE_MISSING_COLUMN.checks: A column the template defines is absent, which includes any template column that has been renamed. Reported once per missing column per layer, so a stripped-down layer produces many at once.

GPKG_BASELINE_COLUMN_SQLITE_TYPE.checks: A column exists with the right name but holds the wrong kind of value — text where a number is expected, or the reverse. Column length is never compared, so a text field of any size passes.

GPKG_BASELINE_COLUMN_NOT_NULL.checks: A column's must-always-have-a-value setting differs from the template. Only the row identifier is required to carry one, so this fires either because it lost that setting or because another column gained it.

GPKG_BASELINE_COLUMN_PRIMARY_KEY.checks: The column acting as the layer's unique row identifier is not the one the template expects.

NO_REDLINE.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
NO_REDLINE.checks: No red line boundary reached the geometry stage. In ordinary use the equivalent structural rule fires first; both are shown to the user as the same message.

GPKG_RLB_NO_POLYGON.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_RLB_NO_POLYGON.checks: The Red Line Boundary layer contains no area shape. Rows with nothing drawn, and rows holding a line or point, do not count towards the total.

GPKG_RLB_TOO_MANY_POLYGONS.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_RLB_TOO_MANY_POLYGONS.checks: The Red Line Boundary layer holds more than one row. What is counted is rows, not separate pieces of land, so a site of several detached areas stored as one multi-part feature passes.

NO_HABITAT_AREAS.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
NO_HABITAT_AREAS.checks: The Habitats layer contains no area shape at all. Also fires when every shape in the layer is the wrong kind, which reads as though the layer were empty.

GPKG_HABITATS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_HABITATS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.checks: The Habitats layer holds at least one valid area shape and also something that is not one — a stray line or point mixed into the same layer.

GPKG_HEDGEROWS_NO_LINESTRING_GEOMETRY.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_HEDGEROWS_NO_LINESTRING_GEOMETRY.checks: The Hedgerows layer has rows but not one usable line among them. An entirely empty optional layer passes; a layer of rows with nothing drawn does not.

GPKG_HEDGEROWS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_HEDGEROWS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.checks: The Hedgerows layer holds at least one valid line and also something that is not a line.

GPKG_RIVERS_NO_LINESTRING_GEOMETRY.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_RIVERS_NO_LINESTRING_GEOMETRY.checks: The Rivers layer has rows but not one usable line among them, on the same terms as Hedgerows.

GPKG_RIVERS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.group: Shapes present and of the right kind
GPKG_RIVERS_WRONG_GEOMETRY_TYPE.checks: The Rivers layer holds at least one valid line and also something that is not a line.

GPKG_RLB_UNREADABLE_GEOMETRY.checks: A row in the Red Line Boundary layer holds shape data that cannot be interpreted at all — truncated or corrupt, rather than badly drawn. One such row stops the rest of that layer's checks.

GPKG_HABITATS_UNREADABLE_GEOMETRY.checks: A row in the Habitats layer holds shape data that cannot be interpreted at all.

GPKG_HEDGEROWS_UNREADABLE_GEOMETRY.checks: A row in the Hedgerows layer holds shape data that cannot be interpreted at all.

GPKG_RIVERS_UNREADABLE_GEOMETRY.checks: A row in the Rivers layer holds shape data that cannot be interpreted at all.

REDLINE_INVALID_GEOMETRY.checks: The red line boundary is recognisable as an area but is not a legal one — most often a bowtie where the outline crosses itself, leaving no consistent answer to what is inside the site. Only the first fault is reported, with its map location.

AREA_PARCELS_INVALID_GEOMETRY.checks: A habitat parcel is not a legal area shape, for the same reasons. Unlike the boundary check, every offending parcel is named, up to fifty.

PARCEL_OVERLAPS.checks: Two habitat parcels claim the same ground. Parcels that merely touch along a shared edge always pass.
PARCEL_OVERLAPS.toleranceIs: An overlap is tolerated up to

SLIVERS_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: Habitat parcel material escaping past the boundary, measured on the parcels as a whole rather than per parcel. Reports a location rather than naming a parcel.

AREA_PARCELS_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: A single habitat parcel escaping past the boundary. Measures escaping area rather than testing containment, so parcels sharing an edge with the boundary are not flagged.

HEDGEROWS_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: Hedgerow length falling outside the boundary. The tolerance is a total across every excursion, not an allowance per excursion.

WATERCOURSES_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: Watercourse length falling outside the boundary, on the same terms as hedgerows.

IGGIS_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: Green infrastructure area escaping past the boundary. Unreachable in ordinary use, and demonstrably so: that layer is not in the template, so the fixture built to exercise this rule is rejected as an unexpected layer before the containment check runs.

TREES_OUTSIDE_REDLINE.checks: A tree sits outside the boundary. Unlike the line rules this is a straight-line distance per tree, so a tree inside or exactly on the boundary passes.

AREA_SUM_MISMATCH.checks: The total area of the habitat parcels differs from the boundary area. The tolerance is absolute rather than proportional, so large sites are harder to pass. Both totals are plain sums, so a gap and an overlap of similar size cancel out and the check stays silent.

REDLINE_OUTSIDE_ENGLAND.checks: Part of the boundary falls outside a reference outline of England. That outline is heavily generalised, so genuinely English coastal and border sites can fail it.

REDLINE_AREA_TOO_LARGE.checks: The boundary encloses more land than any real site plausibly would, so in practice this catches a coordinate system error or a stray vertex.

HABITAT_DISTINCTIVENESS_NOT_IN_SCOPE.checks: A habitat falls in the High or Very High distinctiveness band, which this service does not yet handle. Applies to area habitats, hedgerows and watercourses, and to habitats proposed as well as existing. Around half of all area habitat types are affected, and an ordinary river or stream always is.

DUPLICATE_HABITAT_REF.checks: Two rows in the Habitats layer share a parcel reference. Blank references are ignored, and matching is exact, so references differing only by capitalisation or a trailing space are treated as distinct.

ADVANCE_AND_DELAY_BOTH_SET.checks: One feature carries both advance years and delay years, which the statutory metric forbids as they are opposite directions on the same timeline. Applies to area habitats, hedgerows and watercourses; urban trees are excluded because the service does not read those columns on that layer.

SIZING_FAILED.checks: The database call that measures habitat sizes failed, after the file had already passed every check. Nothing about the upload was wrong.

INVALID_FILE_METADATA.checks: Covers two unrelated situations. The file size or upload reference reported for the upload is outside the allowed bounds, which is the reader's to fix. Or the record built internally from an already-valid file failed its own schema, which is not.

VALIDATION_FAILED.checks: An unexpected fault anywhere in the validation run. Every real rule violation returns its own code instead, so this always indicates a service problem rather than a file problem.

AREA_PARCELS_TOO_SMALL.checks: A single habitat parcel covers less ground than the smallest area a genuine parcel is expected to occupy, marking it as a stray digitising artefact rather than a real habitat. It is judged on area alone, so a long, thin parcel passes as long as its total footprint is large enough.

INVALID_FILENAME.checks: The name of the uploaded file contains a character the service does not accept, or is longer than the allowed length. Letters, numbers, spaces, full stops, underscores, hyphens and round brackets all pass, and the name has to begin with a letter or number; nothing inside the file is looked at.
